solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Call about books used to make hearty dish

indicators.note: about means going round, so the first word wraps around the second

blocks.note: to page someone is to call them over a speaker
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A recipe in which a phone call about books somehow produces a filling meal.
explanation.walkthrough: OT, the Old Testament, is the usual crossword abbreviation for a set of books.
explanation.definitionFit: Potage is a thick, substantial soup, a filling meal served at the table.

clue.text: After spillage I clear up rum

indicators.note: a spillage scatters things, so the following letters land in a new order

blocks.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tidying up after knocking over a bottle of rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like the spilt drink, but it is the old British adjective meaning odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum is informal British for strange or odd, which is what peculiar means.

clue.text: With Sun obscured chap won't!

indicators.note: something obscured is hidden from view, so that letter disappears from the name

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for sun
Stan is a man's name, standing for any chap

explanation.surface: On a cloudy day a man fails to get a suntan.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove S from STAN to leave TAN; read whole, the clue says that without sunshine a chap won't tan.
explanation.definitionFit: Tanning needs sunshine, so with the sun hidden a person does not go brown.

clue.text: Start losing support?

blocks.note: first meaning: fall behind, begin to lag in a race or with payments
second meaning: back or champion a cause

explanation.surface: A question about whether losing heart begins with losing backing.
explanation.walkthrough: The same phrasal verb means to fall into arrears and to throw your weight behind someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting behind means slipping back in a contest, and also lending backing to a person or cause.

clue.text: Yale finally reward American academic no longer in post

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word it follows, keeping only that letter

blocks.note: the last letter of Yale
to merit is to deserve a reward
US is the standard abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: Yale honours a retired American professor at last.
explanation.definitionFit: An emeritus professor is a retired academic who keeps the title after leaving the job.

clue.text: Small check for drinks found here? Possibly not

definitions.text: Small check for drinks found here? Possibly not

blocks.note: mini means small
to bar is to check or prevent

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a little hotel fridge restrains your drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, a 'small check for drinks' is a little restriction on drinking, and the hotel fridge stocked with alcohol is hardly that, hence 'Possibly not'.
explanation.definitionFit: A minibar is a small refrigerator of drinks in a hotel room, where guests help themselves.

clue.text: Inferior player has time off to become teacher

indicators.note: having something off means losing it, so the letter for time is dropped

blocks.note: in British sporting slang a rabbit is a poor player, especially a weak batsman
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A weak sportsman takes a break and becomes a schoolteacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabbi literally means 'my teacher' in Hebrew; a rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher.

clue.text: Uninspired about plot to finally remove loyal Tory in the 1980s

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the next word only
about means surrounding, so the first word goes round what follows

blocks.note: trite means stale and unoriginal
to hatch a scheme is to plot it
the last letter of remove

explanation.surface: A dull conspiracy to finally oust a faithful Conservative of the 1980s.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nods to the 1990 party revolt that unseated Margaret Thatcher; 'to' is only a joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: A Thatcherite was a devoted follower of Margaret Thatcher, Conservative Prime Minister through the 1980s.

clue.text: Surrendered say, to such top players?

definitions.note: adjective describing the players, not a noun for them

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken, so its sound counts rather than its spelling

blocks.note: ceded means surrendered or given up

explanation.surface: A question of whether the top tennis players simply gave up.
explanation.walkthrough: In tournaments the best players are seeded so they do not meet early.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeded describes the strongest competitors, ranked and kept apart in a tournament draw.

clue.text: Dad exercised and took a rest

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father
to exercise a right is to use it

explanation.surface: Father worked out and then had a breather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exercised' suggests a workout, but here it means employed, as in exercising a power.
explanation.definitionFit: To pause is to stop briefly, a short break from activity.

clue.text: Force prisoners onto coach

blocks.note: cons is slang for convicts
to train is to coach

explanation.surface: Inmates being pushed onto a bus for transfer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Onto' puts the prisoners first, ahead of the coach.
explanation.definitionFit: To constrain is to compel or restrict someone, much as force does.

clue.text: Challenge leader of Brexit party

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its front, so only its opening letter is used

blocks.note: the first letter of Brexit
a rave is a large dance party

explanation.surface: Someone takes on the head of the Brexit Party.
explanation.definitionFit: To brave something is to confront or defy it, facing a challenge head on.

clue.text: Fat Queen's supplies of food

blocks.note: lard is pig fat
ER for Elizabeth Regina, with the possessive s

explanation.surface: Talk of the monarch's stocks of cooking fat.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Larders are storerooms or cupboards holding provisions, so they stand for a household's stocks of food.

clue.text: Chop up rare fig tree to get cool

indicators.note: chopping something up cuts it into pieces that can be reassembled differently

blocks.note: the eleven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Instructions for cutting down an unusual fig tree to make things chilly.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrigerate is to chill food or drink, making it cold.

clue.text: Pass cheese around old church – something to accompany it?

definitions.text: Pass cheese around old church – something to accompany it?

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the cheese wraps the following pieces

blocks.note: Brie is a soft French cheese
O is the abbreviation for old
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Handing round cheese at a church gathering and asking what goes with it.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue asks what you might pass along with the cheese: brie baked in a sweet bun is a classic pairing.
explanation.definitionFit: Brioche is a rich French bread that is often served with brie, so it accompanies the cheese.

clue.text: "Goodbye to Berlin"?

blocks.note: surface reading: the title of Christopher Isherwood's 1939 novel of Weimar Berlin
setter's reading: the farewell you would actually say to someone in Berlin, in German

explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make this look like the book title; instead it asks for the German phrase for goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the standard German farewell, literally 'until we see again'.

clue.text: After a time command without heart and commit mass destruction

indicators.note: without heart means the middle of the word is taken out

blocks.note: an era is a period of time
to dictate is to order or command

explanation.surface: A heartless order that eventually leads to wholesale slaughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the command second; 'without heart' removes only the single central letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To eradicate is to wipe out entirely, destroying something completely.

clue.text: Pleased with journalist's last moving column

indicators.note: last points to the closing letter of the possessive word before it
moving letters around shifts them into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the last letter of journalist

explanation.surface: A happy reporter whose final piece was a touching newspaper column.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Column' looks like a newspaper feature but is the architectural kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedestal is the base or support of a column, and can mean the pillar itself.

clue.text: Beastly New Guinean police forbid march around island

definitions.note: a noun phrase: a creature from New Guinea

indicators.note: to police something is to put it in order, so the next word's letters are rearranged
around means surrounding, so the march wraps the island

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
a parade is a march past
IS is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Papua New Guinea's police ban a protest march on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Police' reads as a noun but is a verb. 'Beastly New Guinean' means an animal native to New Guinea.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds of paradise are brilliantly plumed birds found mainly in New Guinea, so the creature is New Guinean.

clue.text: Crazy female led movement out of control

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for female
to run an organisation is to lead it
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A woman heading a political movement that has run wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movement' suggests a political cause, but it is a muscle's involuntary jerk.
explanation.definitionFit: Frantic means wild with worry or haste, close to crazed in its desperate agitation.

clue.text: Book about older fringe performers

indicators.note: a fringe is an edge, so only the outside letters are kept
about means surrounding, so the book goes round what follows

blocks.note: Acts of the Apostles is a book of the Bible
the first and last letters of older

explanation.surface: A volume on veteran performers from the alternative theatre scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fringe' suggests the Edinburgh Fringe festival, fitting the performers, but it selects the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors are people who perform roles on stage or screen.

clue.text: Small wrap contains last of cucumber pickle

indicators.note: last of points to the closing letter of the word after it
contains means holding inside, so the wrap goes round the next letter

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a cape is a sleeveless wrap worn over the shoulders
the last letter of cucumber

explanation.surface: A little tortilla wrap holding a bit of cucumber relish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pickle' looks like a condiment in the sandwich scene, but it means a predicament.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrape is an awkward fix or tight spot, as is a pickle.

clue.text: Revolutionary London college with a top football team

blocks.note: Che Guevara, the archetypal revolutionary
the London School of Economics
taken as written

explanation.surface: A radical student at a London college who supports a leading club.
explanation.definitionFit: Chelsea FC is a leading Premier League football club based in west London.

clue.text: Steps taken to get son a management qualification

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
taken as written
Master of Business Administration

explanation.surface: A parent takes measures so their boy earns a business degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steps' seems to mean measures taken, but it means dance steps.
explanation.definitionFit: The samba is a lively Brazilian dance, a sequence of steps.

clue.text: Engineers enter dock on English warship

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so the engineers sit within the next word

blocks.note: to dock a tail is to trim it
RE is the Royal Engineers
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Army engineers come into an English harbour aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dock' suggests a harbour but means cut short, as with a tail; 'on' in an across clue places the English letter last.
explanation.definitionFit: A trireme was an ancient galley warship with three banks of oars.

clue.text: A large weapon creates panic

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for large
an arm is a weapon, as in firearm

explanation.surface: A big gun causes people to panic.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarm is sudden fear and agitation, a state close to panic.

clue.text: I ignored label put on a massive battle-axe

indicators.note: ignoring the letter I means leaving it out of the word that follows

blocks.note: a term is a label or name
giant means massive

explanation.surface: Someone labels a huge weapon as a battle-axe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Battle-axe' looks like the weapon in the scene, but it is slang for a domineering woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A termagant is a violent, overbearing woman, which battle-axe describes colloquially.

clue.text: Place to leave fruit for parrot

indicators.note: to leave means to go away, so these letters depart from the word

blocks.note: PL is the abbreviation for place
an apple is a fruit

explanation.surface: Somewhere you set down fruit for a pet bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parrot' looks like the bird but is the verb meaning to mimic.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape someone is to imitate them, just as to parrot is to copy.

clue.text: Cheap yet novel pirate equipment

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are made into something new

blocks.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An inexpensive but original pirate costume accessory.
explanation.definitionFit: The patch over one eye is the stock accessory of a stage pirate.

clue.text: Expose the truth about controversial food

blocks.note: re means concerning
veal is controversial because of how calves are raised

explanation.surface: An exposé uncovering the facts about a disputed food product.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal is to disclose or make known what was hidden.
